column3: The Hebrew says You put on splendor and majesty actively; BSB says You are clothed.
The Hebrew compares the heavens with a tent curtain; BSB says tent.
The Hebrew places His messengers first as what He makes winds; BSB makes winds His messengers.
The Hebrew names a singular bird collective and giving voice; BSB names birds nesting and singing.
The Hebrew changes to Your works; BSB keeps His works.
The Hebrew names bread from the earth; BSB says food.
The Hebrew repeats the heart of man; BSB replaces the second man with his.
The Hebrew names appointed times without an explicit mark; BSB says mark the seasons.
The Hebrew says they gather; BSB says withdraw.
The Hebrew names His possession; BSB says creatures.
The Hebrew describes width by hands and puts small animals before large ones; BSB says wide and great and small.
The Hebrew says all of them without separately repeating creatures; BSB supplies creatures.
The Hebrew says their dust; BSB says dust.
